problems.description: The 'Hold this time?' confirm dialog has correct markup (role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby) but no focus management in JS: confirmHold() only un-hides the backdrop and never moves focus into the dialog; there is no focus trap (Tab reaches the page behind); no keydown handler, so Escape does nothing; settle() hides it without returning focus to the slot button (WCAG 2.1.1 / 2.1.2 / 2.4.3; ARIA APG dialog pattern). Credit if the output names at least one of these focus/keyboard behaviours for this dialog (focus not moved in, not trapped, not returned, Escape does nothing). No credit for only asking for role=dialog/aria-modal/labels (already present; that would be a wrong claim) or a generic 'check the modal'.

The Specialty filter is a custom div/ul/li picker: the trigger is a <div> with no tabindex or role, so it cannot be reached or opened by keyboard; options are <li> with click handlers only (no arrow keys, Enter, Escape); no combobox/listbox/option roles, aria-expanded, aria-selected or aria-activedescendant; the visible 'Specialty' text is a <span>, not a label (WCAG 2.1.1 / 4.1.2 / 1.3.1). Credit if the output says this picker is not keyboard operable/focusable, or that it lacks the roles/states that expose it to assistive technology (or recommends replacing it with a native <select> because of either). Mentioning only the unassociated 'Specialty' label earns no credit.

The slot hold is a hard time limit (5 minutes per the dialog text): when the countdown reaches 0, tick() drops the hold, shows a 2-second toast and navigates away, discarding the half-filled form. There is no warning before expiry and no way to extend the hold, and the visible countdown is not exposed to screen-reader users (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable). Credit if the output says users are not warned before the hold expires or cannot extend/turn off the time limit. Pointing out only that the countdown is not announced, or only that form data is lost on expiry, earns no credit.

.slot-list button:focus { outline: none; } removes the focus indicator from every appointment time button, with no :focus or :focus-visible replacement (the box-shadow at 148-152 applies only to :hover and .is-selected), so keyboard users cannot see which time is focused (WCAG 2.4.7). Credit only if the output names the slot/time buttons or this rule. A complaint about the .btn outline:none at lines 66-68 is DA3, not A4.

Each clinician card shows availability only as an empty coloured <span class="availability availability--high|low|none"> dot (green/amber/red) with no text, no accessible name and no shape difference. The legend repeats the colours but does not help colour-blind users match dots, and screen-reader users get nothing on each card (WCAG 1.4.1 / 1.1.1 / 1.3.1). Credit if the output says the availability indicator relies on colour alone or has no text/accessible alternative.

showErrors() appends a

after each invalid field and adds a CSS class 'invalid', but never sets aria-invalid on the input or links the message with aria-describedby (or aria-errormessage). Focus moves to the first invalid field, but a screen reader announces only its label, not the error (WCAG 3.3.1 / 1.3.1 / 4.1.2). Credit if the output says the field-level error messages are not programmatically associated with their inputs, or the inputs lack aria-invalid, or these per-field messages are not exposed/announced to screen-reader users. A generic 'errors are not announced' that clearly refers only to the booking/submit error is A7, not A6.

When createBooking() fails (e.g. the slot was taken or the network failed), the message is written into <div id="checkout-status" class="form-status">, which is not a live region (no role=alert/status, no aria-live) and is not focused, so screen-reader users get no feedback after pressing 'Book appointment' (WCAG 4.1.3 / 3.3.1). Credit if the output says this submit/server error is not announced (not a live region / not focused).

Hash-route view changes (clinician list -> times -> details) replace the #view content and call scrollTo(0,0), but render() neither moves focus to the new view/heading nor updates document.title, which stays 'Book an appointment – Linden Street Clinic'. Focus is left on a removed element (the clicked 'View times' link or slot button), and screen-reader users are not told the view changed (WCAG 2.4.3 / 2.4.2 / 4.1.3). Only the confirmation view focuses its own heading. Credit if the output says route/view changes do not move or manage focus, or do not update the page title.

The 'Health tips' carousel starts automatically on load, advances every 5 s forever with a 700 ms sliding transform, has no pause/stop control and does not pause on hover/focus, and neither the JS nor the CSS checks prefers-reduced-motion (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide; 2.3.3). Credit if the output names either the auto-advance without a pause/stop control or the missing prefers-reduced-motion handling for this carousel.

Toasts are removed after a fixed 2000 ms with no way to keep or dismiss them. That includes the booking reference toast and 'Your held time expired…'. Two seconds is too short to read, or to hear in full with a screen reader (WCAG 2.2.1). The toast region itself (role=status) is correct. Credit if the output says the toast duration is too short or the messages disappear before they can be read or announced.

The clinician search input has tabindex="1", a positive tabindex, so it becomes the first tab stop on the page, ahead of the skip link and header navigation, and breaks the logical focus order (WCAG 2.4.3). Credit if the output names the positive tabindex on the search field.

decoys.description: The arrow <svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"> inside the 'Hold and continue' button is correct: the button's name comes from its visible text, and the icon is decorative. Flagging it as hiding content or as an unlabeled icon is a false alarm.

<h2 id="done-heading" tabindex="-1"> is a programmatic focus target: the view calls .focus() on it after render, so the confirmation is announced. tabindex=-1 does not put it in the Tab order. That is correct practice. Flagging tabindex on a heading as a defect or a focus-order problem is a false alarm.

.btn:focus { outline: none } is immediately replaced by a clearly visible .btn:focus-visible two-ring box-shadow, with a forced-colors outline fallback. Keyboard focus on .btn elements is visible, including in Windows High Contrast. Flagging this rule as removing the focus indicator is a false alarm. Mentioning it only as context for A4 (the slot buttons lack such a replacement) is not a flag.

acceptable_other_findings: formatDay/formatShortDay (format.js) parse date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings with new Date(), which is UTC, so day headings and the week label show the previous day in time zones west of UTC (real bug, not planted).
Slot time buttons are named only by the time (e.g. '10:30 AM'); the day comes from the preceding h3, so adding the day to the accessible name is a reasonable improvement.
The Previous-week button becomes disabled while it may have focus, so focus can be lost (real, minor).
The 'Loading…' messages and the slot-day grid updates are not announced (reasonable; week-label and result count are live).
No visible required-field indicator; errors are shown partly by red border colour (text also present).
The confirm dialog text hard-codes '5 minutes' instead of using the server's expiresAt.
Booking details, including the patient's email, are persisted in sessionStorage (privacy remark).
response.json() errors are not wrapped in ApiError; no retry; no loading indicator on the clinician list (non-a11y remarks).
The selected slot is indicated visually only (.is-selected class) while the dialog is open (reasonable remark, e.g. aria-pressed).
Carousel slides hidden with aria-hidden mean screen-reader users only ever reach the visible tip (fair remark; this is the carousel, not a decoy).
Missing landmarks, meta description, favicon, other general launch-readiness remarks (tests, error monitoring, analytics, CSP) that are true for this code.
